decisive_issues: Cartwright–Jensen–Payne Proposition 3.2 gives inclusions of the Brill–Noether locus into theta translates; the paper explicitly warns that the chosen hypersurfaces need not form a complete set of defining equations. The record therefore does not justify identifying the actual initial degeneration with the union of two coordinate planes and the product ideal (u2+1)(u4+1).

Even for a genuine special fiber, absence of smooth F2-rational points is only failure of a sufficient Hensel-lifting criterion, not a proof that the generic fiber has no Q2-points. A singular residue point may lift. The record supplies no theorem forcing every lift over the proposed circle to reduce to a smooth point.
correctness.summary: The finite-field calculation for the stated ad hoc scheme is not enough to prove the record's geometric identification or non-lifting theorem.
correctness.surviving_fragment: The count that the explicitly written F2 torus scheme has one singular F2-point (and smoother F4-points) may be correct as a standalone finite-field computation, but it is not shown to be the relevant Brill–Noether initial degeneration and does not imply the claimed non-lifting result.

originality.summary: Because the central geometric and Henselian inference fails, originality cannot rescue the research claim. The construction may be a new heuristic model, but it is not a validated theorem.

scientific_value.summary: The finite-field toy calculation can motivate further study, but the advertised scientific conclusion—no class on T lifts over Q2—is unsupported.

limitations: This audit does not prove that lifts exist; it proves that the record's argument does not establish nonexistence.
A valid repair would need the actual initial degeneration (or another necessary reduction condition) and a non-lifting theorem stronger than the smooth-point Hensel criterion.
